intro.title: Debounced Search
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a search input component that fetches and displays results from an API only after the user has stopped typing for a short moment. You will learn the concept of debouncing, which helps improve performance by delaying a function call until after a pause in user input. The main technologies involved are React's useState and useEffect hooks, along with a custom debounce function implemented in TypeScript. This project will teach you how to manage user input efficiently and make controlled API calls.
intro.usecase: Debounced search is essential in any UI where users type to filter or search through data, preventing excessive API calls and improving performance. You'll see this pattern in e-commerce product filters, admin dashboards with real-time data tables, and search bars for large datasets like user directories or content libraries. As a developer, implementing debounced search ensures your applications remain responsive while handling user input efficiently, especially when dealing with backend APIs or computationally expensive filtering operations.
